claims.title: Battle of Ourique
claims.summary: By tradition, Afonso Henriques took the title of king of Portugal after defeating a Muslim army at Ourique, asserting the county's break from the kingdom of Leon.

sources.label: Portugal: The kingdom and the Reconquista

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1139-battle-of-ourique, claim TL:PRT:event:1139:battle-of-ourique, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Recognition of autonomy at Zamora
claims.summary: Alfonso VII of Leon and Castile accepted the autonomy of Afonso Henriques, an early step toward the recognised independence of Portugal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1143-recognition-of-autonomy-at-zamora, claim TL:PRT:event:1143:recognition-of-autonomy-at-zamora, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Lisbon
claims.summary: Afonso Henriques took Santarem and then Lisbon from the Muslims, the latter with the help of crusaders sailing to the Holy Land, advancing the Reconquista to the Tagus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1147-capture-of-lisbon, claim TL:PRT:event:1147:capture-of-lisbon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Papal recognition in Manifestis Probatum
claims.summary: Pope Alexander III confirmed Afonso Henriques as king and recognised Portugal as an independent kingdom under the protection of the Holy See, the founding act of Portuguese sovereignty.

sources.label: Portugal: The kingdom and the Reconquista

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1179-papal-recognition-in-manifestis-probatum, claim TL:PRT:event:1179:papal-recognition-in-manifestis-probatum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Alcanices
claims.summary: King Dinis and Ferdinand IV of Castile confirmed Portuguese possession of the Algarve and fixed the frontier, creating one of the oldest stable borders in Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1297-treaty-of-alcanices, claim TL:PRT:event:1297:treaty-of-alcanices, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Ceuta
claims.summary: Portuguese forces took the North African port of Ceuta, the starting point of overseas expansion and of Prince Henry's interest in exploring the African coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1415-capture-of-ceuta, claim TL:PRT:event:1415:capture-of-ceuta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
claims.summary: Bartolomeu Dias led the first European expedition to round the southern tip of Africa, showing that the Atlantic and Indian oceans were connected and opening the route to Asia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1488-dias-rounds-the-cape-of-good-hope, claim TL:PRT:event:1488:dias-rounds-the-cape-of-good-hope, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
claims.summary: Portugal and Castile divided the unexplored world along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, an agreement that underpinned Portugal's claim to Brazil.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1494-treaty-of-tordesillas, claim TL:PRT:event:1494:treaty-of-tordesillas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
claims.summary: Vasco da Gama sailed around the Cape of Good Hope to Calicut, completing the sea route from western Europe to India and inaugurating direct trade with Asia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1498-vasco-da-gama-reaches-india, claim TL:PRT:event:1498:vasco-da-gama-reaches-india, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cabral reaches Brazil
claims.summary: A fleet under Pedro Alvares Cabral, en route to India, made landfall on the coast of Brazil and claimed it for the Portuguese crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1500-cabral-reaches-brazil, claim TL:PRT:event:1500:cabral-reaches-brazil, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Disaster at Alcacer Quibir
claims.summary: King Sebastian was killed leading a crusade into Morocco, triggering the succession crisis that opened the way to Spanish rule.

sources.label: History of Portugal: Union of Spain and Portugal, 1580-1640

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1578-disaster-at-alcacer-quibir, claim TL:PRT:event:1578:disaster-at-alcacer-quibir, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iberian Union under Philip II
claims.summary: Philip II of Spain occupied Portugal and was accepted as king by the Cortes at Tomar in 1581, uniting the two crowns for sixty years.

sources.label: History of Portugal: Union of Spain and Portugal, 1580-1640

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1580-iberian-union-under-philip-ii, claim TL:PRT:event:1580:iberian-union-under-philip-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Restoration and the House of Braganza
claims.summary: A nationalist revolution proclaimed the duke of Braganza as King John IV, restoring Portuguese independence and founding the Braganza dynasty.

sources.label: History of Portugal: Union of Spain and Portugal, 1580-1640

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1640-restoration-and-the-house-of-braganza, claim TL:PRT:event:1640:restoration-and-the-house-of-braganza, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spain recognises independence
claims.summary: By the Treaty of Lisbon, Spain at last acknowledged Portuguese sovereignty, ending the war of Restoration begun in 1640.

sources.label: History of Portugal: Union of Spain and Portugal, 1580-1640

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1668-spain-recognises-independence, claim TL:PRT:event:1668:spain-recognises-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The great Lisbon earthquake
claims.summary: An earthquake, tsunami and fire destroyed much of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands, prompting the reconstruction and reforms directed by the Marquis of Pombal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1755-the-great-lisbon-earthquake, claim TL:PRT:event:1755:the-great-lisbon-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Court flees to Brazil
claims.summary: As a French army invaded, the prince regent and royal court sailed for Brazil under British escort, moving the seat of the Portuguese monarchy to Rio de Janeiro.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1807-court-flees-to-brazil, claim TL:PRT:event:1807:court-flees-to-brazil, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Peninsular War
claims.summary: British, Portuguese and Spanish forces fought the French in the Iberian Peninsula, eventually expelling Napoleon's armies from Portugal and Spain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1808-the-peninsular-war, claim TL:PRT:event:1808:the-peninsular-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of Brazil
claims.summary: Pedro, regent and son of John VI, declared Brazil independent and became its emperor, ending Portugal's rule over its largest and wealthiest colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1822-independence-of-brazil, claim TL:PRT:event:1822:independence-of-brazil, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Salazar and the Estado Novo
claims.summary: Antonio de Oliveira Salazar, prime minister from 1932, built an authoritarian corporative dictatorship, the Estado Novo, that ruled Portugal for over four decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1932-salazar-and-the-estado-novo, claim TL:PRT:event:1932:salazar-and-the-estado-novo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Olivenca dispute
claims.summary: Spain occupied Olivenca in 1801 and acquired it by the Treaty of Badajoz; the Congress of Vienna recommended its return to Portugal in 1815, but the sovereignty remains contested.

sources.label: Written question on the Olivenca issue (Portugal/Spain) and the Ajuda Bridge, E-1298/2003

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1801-the-olivenca-dispute, claim TL:PRT:event:1801:the-olivenca-dispute, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Carnation Revolution
claims.summary: Officers of the Armed Forces Movement overthrew the Estado Novo in a nearly bloodless coup, ending the dictatorship and beginning Portugal's transition to democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1974-the-carnation-revolution, claim TL:PRT:event:1974:the-carnation-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decolonisation of the African empire
claims.summary: Following the revolution, Portugal's African colonies, including Angola and Mozambique, became independent in 1975, ending an empire begun in 1415.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1975-decolonisation-of-the-african-empire, claim TL:PRT:event:1975:decolonisation-of-the-african-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Communities
claims.summary: Portugal joined the European Communities on 1 January 1986, together with Spain, anchoring its democracy in European integration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Portugal: From a frontier county of the Reconquista to a seaborne empire, holding one of Europe's oldest borders.", terralore.co/country/PRT/chronicle#ev-1986-accession-to-the-european-communities, claim TL:PRT:event:1986:accession-to-the-european-communities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Savage Islands maritime dispute
claims.summary: Spain disputed the exclusive economic zone Portugal claims around the Savage Islands, contending that the islets are rocks under the law of the sea, an issue examined in US State Department maritime studies.

sources.label: Limits in the Seas No. 155, Portugal: Maritime Claims and Boundaries
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of Ocean and Polar Affairs
